about: The pictures a tenant or one of its themes may replace. Composer's Assets tab reads this file from the build, offers each slot for upload and, on release, writes the chosen files into `brands`. The game looks a picture up here by its default file: a theme's picture first, then the tenant's, then the default. Only pictures change: the fruits' sizes and paths, the cut, the juice colours and the maths stay the same for everyone. Each slot's prompt describes the current picture for an image generator; the part in square brackets is what a tenant or theme changes.

guide.title: How a set of pictures works
lines: Pick the tenant (and the theme, if the pictures are for one) in the top bar. Everything you upload belongs to that choice.
A theme only needs the pictures it changes: anything it leaves out comes from its tenant, and anything the tenant leaves out comes from the game.
Start every picture from the current one: Download gives you the file the game draws now, at its size. Keep the canvas size and the transparent background.

Every picture comes with a prompt for an image generator. Change the part in [square brackets] to the tenant's or theme's subject and keep the rest: it holds the view, the size and the framing the game needs.
Upload PNG, WebP or JPG. Composer stores it as PNG. Keep each file under 8 MB.
A picture must keep the proportions of the one it replaces. A different size with the same proportions is fine: the game scales it.

guide.title: Fruits: whole, then two halves
lines: Nine fruits fly up; a cut splits one into its two halves and shows what is inside. Each fruit is three pictures, replaced together: Whole, Left half and Right half.
The sections are numbered, not named: a tenant's Fruit 1 need not be a watermelon. The fruit in each prompt is only the game's own one; change it to whatever the tenant's fruit is.

All three share one 1024 × 1024 canvas. The whole fruit is centred at (512, 512) and fills about 72% of the canvas; each half sits exactly where it was in the whole fruit, with its flat cut edge straight down the middle (x = 512) and the other half of the canvas empty.

Make them in SpriteCook: generate the whole fruit first (detailed art, model gemini-3.1-flash-image, transparent background, smart crop off), then make each half by editing that whole fruit (Edit with the whole as the source) with the half's prompt, so size, light and outline match.
The juice and the trail are drawn by the game in the fruit's colours. A replacement fruit should keep a similar flesh colour, or the juice will not match it.
Before the cut, every fruit looks ordinary: no glow, cracks or sparks that hint at what is inside.

guide.title: Inside the fruit
lines: What a cut reveals: Gold is a win, the Bomb ends the round, Rotten is a near miss. They are drawn over the opened fruit, so keep them clearly different in colour and shape, centred, with a transparent margin.

guide.title: The street
lines: Each atmosphere is three layers: the sky fills the screen behind everything, and the two house layers stand pinned to the left and right edges, so wide screens spread them apart. Replace all three of an atmosphere together.
Keep the middle of the sky empty: fruit flies there and the multiplier is shown there.

The player picks Day or Sunset for the next session. Sunset is the day street relit: make it in SpriteCook by editing each day layer (model gemini-3-pro-image) with a sunset prompt, keeping shapes and framing, then keep each layer at the day layer's size.

guide.title: Wins and hints
lines: The coin spills out of a gold core on a win; the win-rain coin falls with the fruit on a big win; the BOOM sticker shows when the bomb goes off; the hand shows a new player how to swipe.
The BOOM sticker carries its word in the picture, so spell it exactly as the tenant wants it read.

slots.title: Thumbnail
slots.prompt: A square game thumbnail for Fruit Boom, 512 × 512 px, shown as the game's tile in an app's lobby, on the showcase and in link previews: [the game's hero and its world in one bold, readable picture, with the game's name Fruit Boom in big playful letters]. Bright, saturated cartoon mobile-game art, thick dark outlines, soft cel shading, light from the top left. Fills the square edge to edge, no rounded corners, no border, no transparent margins.
